subject: DPA - TOMs exhibit: encryption, key management, and execution pathway
messages:
From: Claudia Santos <claudia.santos@sigmafinance.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: sigma-legal@sigmafinance.com
Date: 2027-04-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: TOMs exhibit — encryption approach and BYOK options

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. As we start DPA redlines I wanted to confirm a few items for our security team so we can move to internal sign-off:

- Clarify whether Redwood will support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for hosted deployments, and if so whether those keys can be backed by an HSM (FIPS 140-2/3).
- If BYOK is available, what is the key-escrow policy and the mechanics for key rotation/rollback? We need to understand ability to revoke access and emergency key rotation windows.
- Request explicit wording for access controls: which Redwood roles/systems have administrative key access, and how are access requests audited?
- Ask for an up-to-date subprocessor manifest and typical notification lead time for new subprocessors (we prefer 30 days).
- Evidence: a short artifact listing audit-log retention, KMS audit hooks, and whether cryptographic material is exported for backups.

Can you share a redline of the TOMs exhibit that captures BYOK language plus the above operational details? Also please confirm the preferred execution method — Sigma uses DocuSign by default but happy to accept AdobeSign if that is easier on your side.

Best,
Claudia Santos
Head of Data Protection
Sigma Finance

Attachment: subprocessors_request_template.csv (stub)

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Claudia Santos <claudia.santos@sigmafinance.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: TOMs exhibit — encryption approach and BYOK options

Hi Claudia — thanks for the clear list. Appreciate the prioritization.

We can accommodate your BYOK request for hosted deployments with a customer-managed keys (BYOK) path that leverages third-party KMS (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / Google KMS). For higher assurance we offer HSM-backed keys via BYOK integrations; we will call this out in Section 3.2 of the TOMs exhibit.

High level bullets we will add to the TOMs exhibit redline:
- BYOK supported for hosted and dedicated; HSM-backed keys supported when customer supplies a compatible Cloud KMS with HSM guarantee.
- Key rotation: customer-triggered and scheduled rotation supported; Redwood will not retain plaintext key material. Rotation rollback requires a signed emergency request and can be actioned within a 4-hour window for critical incidents.
- Access controls: list of internal roles with key-administration privileges (Security Ops, Platform Eng on a least-privilege basis); all key-access actions are logged to our KMS audit stream and forwarded to customer audit sinks on request.
- Subprocessor notification: standard is 45 days; we can offer 30 days as a commercial concession for Sigma.
- Evidence package: we will attach an audit matrix with SOC 2 logging, KMS event retention (90 days default, extendable), and a KMS diagram showing separation of control.

I am attaching the initial redline (TOMs_Exhibit_redline_v1.docx). If that looks reasonable we can prepare a DocuSign packet and route it to Sigma legal. Would you prefer DocuSign or AdobeSign?

Note: tagging @priyom_das for technical correctness and @marcus_lin on product implications.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Senior Sales Manager, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: TOMs_Exhibit_redline_v1.docx (redline of exhibit)

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T13:45:00Z
Subject: Re: TOMs exhibit — encryption approach and BYOK options

Avery / team — quick technical clarifications to feed into the redline before sending externally:

> "HSM-backed keys supported when customer supplies a compatible Cloud KMS with HSM guarantee."
- Suggest we add specific supported configurations: AWS KMS with CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault with HSM-protected keys, Google Cloud KMS with CMEK/HSM.

> "Rotation rollback requires a signed emergency request and can be actioned within a 4-hour window for critical incidents."
- Ops note: we can commit to a 4-hour emergency rotation assistance SLA for customers on Dedicated or Private plans. For Hosted (standard) customers, operational assistance will be on a best-effort unless covered by a dedicated contract. Recommend conditional language in 3.2 that ties emergency rotation SLA to the customer's contract tier.

> "Key-access actions are logged to our KMS audit stream and forwarded to customer audit sinks on request."
- We should specify retention: default 90 days in-host, 365 days available for enterprise add-on. Also note we push KMS event metadata (no plaintext keys) to customer SSE-enabled buckets on request.

I attached a short evidence bulletin (evidence_bulletin_kms_diagram.pdf) we can share as an appendix. Also propose a small wording change for Section 3.2 to avoid implying Redwood 'stores' key material — we explicitly do not persist customer key material for BYOK.

— Priyom

Attachment: evidence_bulletin_kms_diagram.pdf (diagram + retention bullets)

From: Claudia Santos <claudia.santos@sigmafinance.com>

Thanks Avery and Priyom — that helps. Two quick asks from legal/security before we proceed to execution: 

1) Please include explicit contract language that Redwood will not have the ability to decrypt customer data when BYOK is in use and will not retain plaintext key material.
2) Please provide the up-to-date subprocessor manifest (CSV) and confirm that new subprocessor notifications will be 30 days for Sigma as discussed.

If those are in the redline I can share with our internal counsel and we should be able to route for signature. Please provide the redline that includes the conditional SLA language Priyom mentioned so our procurement team can see the differences between Hosted vs Dedicated.

Also, we'll want the DocuSign packet to include: DPA master agreement (exhibit A), TOMs exhibit redline, and the subprocessor manifest.

Claudia
